title: Flat resolutions for a fixed finite filtration
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a small ringed site, with $\mathcal O$ commutative and module values in an ambient universe containing the site. Use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], flat module sheaves [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and K-flat complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Fix integers $a\le b$. Give complexes decreasing filtrations by subcomplexes, equal to the whole complex for $p\le a$ and zero for $p>b$, and invert the chain maps that are quasi-isomorphisms on every graded quotient. Every bounded-above such filtered complex $M$ admits a termwise strict epimorphism $P\to M$ that is a filtered quasi-isomorphism, where $P$ is bounded above and, in each cochain degree, its filtered module is a split finite sum of flat module sheaves placed in grades $a,\ldots,b$. Here strict epimorphism means that $F^pP\to F^pM$ is an epimorphism for every $p$. The splittings need not commute with differentials. Every graded complex of $P$ and its underlying unfiltered complex are K-flat. The localization of the homotopy category of these bounded-above split-flat filtered complexes at filtered quasi-isomorphisms maps equivalently to the bounded-above finite filtered derived category; these equivalences are compatible with inclusions of filtration intervals. If $W$ is any finite filtered complex acyclic on every graded quotient and $P$ is such a split-flat model, the total tensor complex with the convolution filtration $F^r\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes W)=\sum_{p+q=r}\operatorname{im}\operatorname{Tot}(F^pP\otimes F^qW)$ is again acyclic on every graded quotient. The same assertion holds with the two tensor factors reversed.

source.place: §5.2.1(b), filtered tensor construction referenced to Illusie V §2. The fixed finite filtered flat-resolution formulation is an agent-formulated resolution tool, not a verbatim assertion of this paragraph. Unfiltered ingredients: literature/stacks-project/sites-cohomology.tex, Tags 077J (lemma-resolution-by-direct-sums-extensions-by-zero, bounded-above resolutions), 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution) and 06YQ (lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat). The finite filtered extension is described in report.md; Illusie I, V §2 is WANTED.

proof.text: Work in the abelian category $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For any filtered module $E$ with the fixed bounds, choose flat epimorphisms $B_j\twoheadrightarrow F^jE$ for $a\le j\le b$, using [lem-pc-sites-modules-functorial-flat-cover]. Put $Q(E)=\bigoplus_{j=a}^b B_j$ with $F^pQ(E)=\bigoplus_{j\ge p}B_j$ and map it to $E$ by summing the chosen maps followed by inclusions. This is filtration preserving. Its restriction to $F^p$ is an epimorphism since the summand $B_p$ already maps epimorphically to $F^pE$; for $p<a$ use $B_a$, and for $p>b$ both sides are zero. Its grade $j$ is $B_j$. No lifting property of a flat module is asserted: this construction uses covers of the filtration steps, not lifts of maps from graded quotients.

source.place: Tag 03EW (lemma-module-quotient-flat), applied to the finitely many filtration steps; explicit finite-sum construction

proof.text:
Choose $N$ with $M^n=0$ for $n>N$. Set $P^n=0$ and $f^n=0$ there. We construct $P^n,d_P^n,f^n$ by descending induction. The induction invariant, in addition to the chain-map equations already defined, is that $Z^{n+1}(F^pP)\to Z^{n+1}(F^pM)$ is an epimorphism for every $p$; it holds initially in degree $N+1$, where both are zero. Here $Z^i$ denotes the kernel of the outgoing differential. Define the module $T^n$ by the equations
$$T^n=\{(x,y)\in M^n\oplus P^{n+1}:d_P^{n+1}y=0,\ f^{n+1}y=d_M^nx\},\qquad F^pT^n=T^n\cap(F^pM^n\oplus F^pP^{n+1}).$$
This is an intersection of kernels in $\mathcal A$ and has the same finite filtration bounds. The projection $F^pT^n\to F^pM^n$ is an epimorphism: it is the pullback of the epimorphism $Z^{n+1}(F^pP)\to Z^{n+1}(F^pM)$ along $d_M^n$, which lands in the latter kernel because $d_M^2=0$. This is the elementary pullback-of-an-epimorphism calculation in an abelian category: the kernel of the pullback projection identifies with the kernel of the original epimorphism and its image is the entire target.

source.place: Tag 077J (lemma-resolution-by-direct-sums-extensions-by-zero), bounded-above resolution construction made explicit for a fixed finite flag

proof.text: Apply the finite-sum cover of step 1 to $T^n$, using flat covers of each $F^jT^n$ from [lem-pc-sites-modules-functorial-flat-cover], and call the source $P^n$. Compose $P^n\to T^n$ with its first and second projections to define $f^n$ and $d_P^n$. The two defining equations of $T^n$ give $d_P^{n+1}d_P^n=0$ and $f^{n+1}d_P^n=d_M^nf^n$. All maps preserve every $F^p$, and $F^pP^n\to F^pM^n$ is epimorphic by step 2. The subobject $Z^n(F^pM)$ maps into $F^pT^n$ by $x\mapsto(x,0)$. Pulling back the epimorphism $F^pP^n\to F^pT^n$ along this map gives an epimorphism onto $Z^n(F^pM)$; its source maps into $Z^n(F^pP)$ since the second coordinate is zero. Thus the cycle epimorphism required for the next induction step holds. Induction on $N-n\in\mathbf N$ now defines the whole complex, with no choice at an infinite upper end. Every $P^n$ has the required split-flat finite filtration and $P$ vanishes above $N$.

source.place: Tag 077J (lemma-resolution-by-direct-sums-extensions-by-zero), downward construction using Tag 03EW at each degree

proof.text: Let $K=\ker(f:P\to M)$ with its induced filtration. For each $p,n$, a cycle $z$ in $F^pK^{n+1}$ defines the pair $(0,z)$ in $F^pT^n$. Pulling $F^pP^n\twoheadrightarrow F^pT^n$ back to these pairs gives epimorphic lifts $x$ with $f^nx=0$ and $d_P^nx=z$. Consequently $d:F^pK^n\to Z^{n+1}(F^pK)$ is an epimorphism, and $F^pK$ is acyclic. These are image/kernel calculations, so the lifts mean epimorphic base changes, not surjectivity on sections of an arbitrary site object. The sequence $0\to F^pK\to F^pP\to F^pM\to0$ is termwise short exact. Its cohomology sequence [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] shows that $F^pf$ is a quasi-isomorphism for every $p$.

source.place: Tag 077J (lemma-resolution-by-direct-sums-extensions-by-zero), acyclic-kernel verification for every filtration step

proof.text:
Termwise strict surjectivity of $f$ implies
$$0\to\operatorname{gr}^pK\to\operatorname{gr}^pP\to\operatorname{gr}^pM\to0.$$
Indeed, if a representative $x\in F^pP$ maps into $F^{p+1}M$, use the epimorphism $F^{p+1}P\to F^{p+1}M$ to subtract a lift; the difference lies in $F^pK$. The kernel of $F^pK\to\operatorname{gr}^pP$ is precisely $F^{p+1}K$. These statements again mean images in the abelian category. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] first to $0\to F^{p+1}K\to F^pK\to\operatorname{gr}^pK\to0$: both filtration steps of $K$ are acyclic by step 4, so its grade is acyclic. Apply it a second time to the displayed sequence: $\operatorname{gr}^pf$ is a quasi-isomorphism. This proves that the constructed strict epimorphism is a filtered quasi-isomorphism, rather than merely an underlying quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 05S1 (lemma-filtered-acyclic), graded quasi-isomorphisms; direct strict-kernel calculation and the long exact cohomology sequence

proof.text: In each degree the underlying module $P^n$ and every $(F^pP)^n$ are finite sums of the flat summands chosen in step 3, and $(\operatorname{gr}^pP)^n$ is one of those summands. A finite sum is flat because tensor distributes over finite sums [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], and the sum of a finite family of exact sequences is exact (kernels and images are their finite sums). All these complexes vanish above $N$. Therefore [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] makes $P$, every $F^pP$, and every $\operatorname{gr}^pP$ K-flat. In particular the two K-flatness assertions in the item hold. This uses the bounded-above theorem, not the existence theorem for unbounded K-flat replacements.

Let $\mathcal H$ be the homotopy category of bounded-above complexes with filtrations in $[a,b]$. To check the cone-calculus hypotheses, form the dg category with degree-$r$ maps $\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}_F(X^i,Y^{i+r})$ and differential $\partial h=d_Yh-(-1)^rhd_X$. Closed degree-zero maps are filtered chain maps and boundaries are filtered homotopies. Zero and direct sums give (A) of [lem-coef-dg-abc-homotopy-category-triangulated]. The shift has $X[r]^i=X^{i+r}$ and $d_{X[r]}=(-1)^rd_X$; it sends a degree-$s$ map $h$ to $(-1)^{rs}h$ with shifted indices. This commutes with $\partial$, preserves composition, and composes by addition of shifts. Reindexing identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_F(X,Y[r])$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_F(X,Y)[r]$: in degree $s$ both differentials are $(-1)^rd_Yh-(-1)^shd_X$. This gives (B). For (C), take $C(f)^i=Y^i\oplus X^{i+1}$ with the direct-sum filtration and differential $(y,x)\mapsto(d_Yy+fx,-d_Xx)$. With section $s(x)=(0,x)$ and projection $\pi(y,x)=y$, $\pi\partial s=f$, so this graded splitting has boundary $f[1]$ as (C) requires. These complexes remain bounded above and in the fixed interval. Thus that theorem makes $\mathcal H$ triangulated with cone triangles. Increase the universe to make this dg category small.

Let $\mathcal S\subset\mathcal H$ consist of graded-acyclic complexes. Taking grades commutes with shifts, direct sums, filtered homotopies, and the displayed cone, since the cone filtration is a direct sum. A homotopy equivalence therefore induces homotopy equivalences on all grades, so $\mathcal S$ is replete. If $X,Y\in\mathcal S$, then each $\operatorname{gr}^pC(f)$ is the cone of a map between acyclic complexes. The split short exact cone sequence and [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] make it acyclic. Thus $\mathcal S$ is a full triangulated subcategory containing zero. By [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic], the class of arrows whose cone is in $\mathcal S$ is exactly the filtered quasi-isomorphisms $W$. Apply [lem-trf-triangulated-subcategory-cone-system]: $W$ admits a right calculus of fractions on $\mathcal H$. No assertion about unbounded filtrations or an abelian category of filtered objects is needed.

source.place: Tags 05S1 (lemma-filtered-acyclic) and 05RG (lemma-construct-multiplicative-system), restricted to the fixed interval and bounded-above complexes

proof.text:
Let $\mathcal B$ be the full subcategory of $\mathcal H$ on bounded-above complexes whose filtered modules are degreewise split finite sums of flat sheaves in the stipulated grades. Its maps are all filtered chain maps modulo filtered homotopies, exactly the full subcategory meant in [lem-trf-right-fraction-dense-subcategory]. Steps 1–5 give a denominator $P\to M$ with $P\in\mathcal B$ for every $M\in\mathcal H$; step 8 supplies the right calculus on $\mathcal H$. That lemma now gives the equivalence
$$\mathcal B[(W\cap\operatorname{Arrows}(\mathcal B))^{-1}]\longrightarrow\mathcal H[W^{-1}].$$

Let $\mathcal K$ be the category of bounded-above filtered complexes and filtered chain maps in $[a,b]$, and $q:\mathcal K\to\mathcal H$ its quotient by filtered homotopy [def-trf-split-flat-filtered-sheaf-models]. It is full and surjective on objects. Let $V$ be the filtered homotopy equivalences; $q$ inverts them. If $qf=qg$, choose a filtered $k$ with $f-g=dk+kd$. Use the direct-sum filtered cylinder $I(X)^n=X^n\oplus X^{n+1}\oplus X^n$, with differential $(x,y,z)\mapsto(dx+y,-dy,dz-y)$, sections $i_0(x)=(x,0,0)$, $i_1(x)=(0,0,x)$, and projection $\pi(x,y,z)=x+z$. All remain bounded above and in $[a,b]$. The equations $\pi i_0=\pi i_1=1$ hold, and $h(x,y,z)=(0,-z,0)$ satisfies $1-i_0\pi=dh+hd$, so $\pi\in V$. Finally $H(x,y,z)=fx+ky+gz$ is a filtered chain map: the coefficient of $y$ in $Hd-dH$ is $f-g-kd-dk=0$; its composites with the sections are $f,g$. These verify exactly the cylinder hypotheses of [lem-trf-full-quotient-cylinder-localization], so $q$ is a localization at $V$.

source.place: Functor.isLocalization_of_essSurj_of_full_of_exists_cylinders, lines 78–90; explicit filtered cylinder as in Stacks derived.tex Tag 013N (lemma-make-injective)

proof.text: Every $v\in V$ is a filtered quasi-isomorphism: its filtered homotopy inverse induces a homotopy inverse on every grade, whose cohomology maps are inverse since $dh+hd$ induces zero on cohomology. Thus $V\subset W$. By step 10 and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], a functor $\mathcal K\to\mathcal E$ inverting $W$ factors through $q$; the resulting functor on $\mathcal H$ inverts the homotopy classes represented by $W$, so it factors through $\mathcal H[W^{-1}]$. The same two universal properties give unique lifts of natural transformations. Consequently $\mathcal K\to\mathcal H[W^{-1}]$ is itself a localization at $W$. Uniqueness in the cited node identifies $\mathcal H[W^{-1}]$ with $\mathcal K[W^{-1}]$, the bounded-above fixed-interval filtered derived category defined in [def-trf-uniform-finite-filtered-localization]. Together with step 9, this gives the requested equivalence induced by inclusion of the split-flat models. No lifting of maps from flat sheaves across epimorphisms is used.

source.place: Tags 04VG (lemma-properties-left-localization), 04VK (lemma-properties-right-localization); composition of the displayed universal properties, with natural transformations as in the cited node

proof.text: For an inclusion $[a,b]\subseteq[a',b']$, a filtered complex with the smaller bounds is the same filtered complex with the wider permitted bounds; no reindexing is performed. This inclusion sends split-flat objects to split-flat objects (use zero summands in the new grades) and preserves filtered quasi-isomorphisms. The square of the two inclusions of split-flat homotopy categories into all filtered homotopy categories commutes before localization. Its induced square commutes up to the unique comparison isomorphism after localization by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], since both composites have that same precomposition. The equivalences of steps 9–11 are precisely the functors induced by these inclusions, so they are compatible with interval inclusions. The same uniqueness makes these comparisons coherent for nested intervals.

source.place: Tag 04VG (lemma-properties-left-localization), universal property; natural-transformation clause of the cited node

proof.text: For the tensor assertion, exact filtered colimits and all small colimits in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ are supplied by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian]. In particular, countable direct sums are exact: write the sum as the filtered colimit over finite subsets of the index set of the finite sums, take the corresponding finite sums of a family of short exact sequences, and apply exactness of that filtered colimit. The index category of finite subsets is small in the module universe. It follows that taking a quotient or a kernel in a countable direct sum of short exact sequences gives the direct sum of the corresponding quotients or kernels. This justifies passage to graded quotients in the direct-sum total complexes below; no finite-dimensionality or boundedness assumption on $W$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits), exact filtered colimits; direct sums expressed as filtered colimits of finite sums

proof.text:
Write the degreewise splitting as $P^i=\bigoplus_{j=a}^bB_j^i$. For each $i,k,r$, the convolution submodule of $P^i\otimes W^k$ is
$$\bigoplus_{j=a}^b B_j^i\otimes F^{r-j}W^k.$$
To see this, expand $F^pP^i=\bigoplus_{j\ge p}B_j^i$. The terms with $p+q=r$ and $j\ge p$ lie in the displayed summand because $q=r-p\ge r-j$; conversely that summand occurs for $p=j,q=r-j$. Flatness [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] makes $B_j^i\otimes F^qW^k\to B_j^i\otimes W^k$ injective and gives quotient $B_j^i\otimes\operatorname{gr}^qW^k$. Thus the $r$-th grade in bidegree $(i,k)$ is $\bigoplus_j B_j^i\otimes\operatorname{gr}^{r-j}W^k$. Finite tensor additivity is [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]; step 13 permits taking this quotient through the countable sum $i+k=n$. These are degreewise decompositions; no splitting of complexes is assumed.

source.place: Tag 03ER (definition-flat), tensor exactness; direct verification of the convolution associated grade, with total-complex convention Tag 06YL

proof.text:
The degreewise identification of step 14 is an identification of complexes:
$$\operatorname{gr}^r\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes W)\cong\bigoplus_{j=a}^b\operatorname{Tot}(\operatorname{gr}^jP\otimes\operatorname{gr}^{r-j}W).$$
Indeed, $d_P$ sends a summand of grade $j$ only to grades $l\ge j$. If $l>j$, its tensor with $F^{r-j}W$ lies in filtration $r+1$ since $l+(r-j)\ge r+1$, so it vanishes in grade $r$. The surviving diagonal block is exactly $d_{\operatorname{gr}^jP}$, while the other differential is $(-1)^i d_W$ on cochain bidegree $(i,k)$, as in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. This checks the differential without choosing a chain-compatible splitting. Every $\operatorname{gr}^{r-j}W$ is acyclic by hypothesis, and every $\operatorname{gr}^jP$ is K-flat by step 6. The definition [def-pc-kflat-complex] makes each summand on the right acyclic; apply the explicit cochain swap of step 16 to put the K-flat factor second. That swap and its chain-map check are independent of the acyclicity conclusion. A finite sum of acyclic complexes is acyclic since its cycles and boundaries are the finite sums of the cycles and boundaries. This proves the assertion with $P$ first.

source.place: Tag 06YN (definition-K-flat), and the explicit grade calculation for the convolution filtration

proof.text: The symmetry of sheaf tensor [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] induces a chain isomorphism $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes W)\to\operatorname{Tot}(W\otimes P)$, sending a tensor in bidegree $(i,k)$ to $(-1)^{ik}$ times its swap. With the total differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], the two terms of the chain-map equation have signs $(-1)^{(i+1)k}$ and $(-1)^i(-1)^{i(k+1)}$ after swapping, which equal the corresponding signs $(-1)^{ik+k}$ and $(-1)^{ik}$ on the other side. This isomorphism exchanges the convolution summand indexed by $(p,q)$ with the one indexed by $(q,p)$, so it preserves each $F^r$ and induces isomorphisms on grades. The reversed tensor product is therefore graded acyclic as well. Empty or zero complexes cause no exception, and for $a=b$ the construction and all formulas have just one filtration grade.

source.place: Tag 06YL, tensor total-complex convention; Koszul symmetry calculation
